title: Anchorless sprint notes — KPI experiments & weekly check-ins
content:
Purpose: quick, messy weekly scratch for keeping my personal KPIs tangible during chaotic weeks. Not a finalized plan — just a running log of experiments, outcomes, and short actions.

Context: I'm the product PM on hosted API features for small customers. My macro objective this quarter is to reduce onboarding friction for PLG users and raise meaningful activation. Personal hypothesis: small, repeatable writerly behaviors (doc sprints, PR microtasks, 2 pairing sessions / week) will push the activation needle via clearer docs + faster rollouts.

Top-level personal KPIs (6-week horizon)
- Active experiments: 3 parallel (onboarding flow docs, sample-app eval harness, small default prompt templates)
- Target metrics by end of sprint-window:
  * Docs drafts published: 3 -> target 3
  * PRs merged with docs + sample: 6 -> target 6
  * Review turnaround (my owned PRs): median < 24h -> target 24h
  * Informal user walkthroughs scheduled: 4 -> target 4

Weekly check-in (week 3 snapshot)
- Wins:
  * Published first draft of sample-app README (short, opinionated + code snippet). Got positive initial feedback from Marco.
  * Paired with eng on the eval harness; prototype generates embeddings locally for a tiny dataset.
- Misses / friction:
  * Spent too much time formatting examples; timebox failed twice.
  * Only 1 user walkthrough scheduled (target 4). Need to convert slack interest into calendar invites.

Hypotheses to validate (short bullets)
1) If I ship 3 short, example-driven docs, new sign-ups will show +10% higher completion of the quickstart within 7 days. (Metric: quickstart completion rate)
2) If the eval harness includes a pre-built prompts folder, trial users will be more likely to run an eval (Metric: eval-run events per new account).
3) If I shorten PR size (<=200 LOC), review time will drop and merge frequency will increase (Metric: PR merge rate / reviewer latency).

Experiments running (status + next steps)
- Onboarding doc sprint: status = draft; next = trim examples to one canonical flow; ask Rina to sanity-check phrasing (deadline Tue).
- Sample-app README: status = published (v0.1); next = create 2-minute demo video + attach to README.
- Eval harness bootstrap: status = prototype; next = add telemetry event when eval-run completes, file ticket JIRA-7812 for instrumentation.

Signals I’ll watch (leading + lagging)
- Leading: number of quickstart clicks, README open events, demo watch rate
- Lagging: conversion to trial-to-paid, eval-run completions, number of feedback threads mentioning docs

Personal behavior interventions (micro-habits for the next 2 weeks)
- 45-minute focused doc block M/W/F (calendar blocked)
- Two 30-minute pairing sessions each week (one engineering, one docs/editorial)
- Daily 10-min PR triage at end of day (clear small comments)

Risks / failure modes (quick list)
- Over-optimizing for docs format instead of content (beautiful but not actionable). Mitigation: lean on product dev to test in 1:1 demos.
- Getting pulled into big cross-team meetings; habit: send a 1-line agenda before accepting requests, decline if not aligned to immediate KPI.

Quick retro notes (what I learned this sprint)
- Short, opinionated examples reduce cognitive load for reviewers — saved ~30 minutes per review on average.
- Pairing early (before PR) avoids rework — invest more front-loaded time.

Next three concrete actions (today/tomorrow)
1) Trim onboarding doc to single canonical flow; ping Rina for a quick review (today).
2) Add telemetry event to eval harness prototype; open JIRA-7812 with acceptance criteria (tomorrow).
3) Schedule four user walkthrough slots and post an invite in #hosted-api (by EOD Friday).

Open questions / decisions needed
- Which metric is highest fidelity for activation? Quickstart completion or first API call? (Ask growth team — link: CON-2342)
- Should sample-app demo be video first or a live workshop? I suspect video scales better but workshop gives richer feedback.

Notes-to-self (short)
- Timebox formatting to 20 minutes — content > cosmetics.
- If pairing yield is low twice in a row, change pairing partners.
- Keep this file lightweight; port stable decisions to Confluence page (CON-2342).

Slack references: #hosted-api, DM Rina, thread Marco -> see github PR link above.

End-of-file: quick mood (0–10): 6 — fatigued but optimistic.

Fragmented ideas to try later:
- Tiny onboarding microcopy A/B: ‘Start in 2 minutes’ vs ‘Start for free’ (hypothesis: clarity beats promotion).
- Small checklist embedded in README that is atomic: 1) run example, 2) make <1 change to prompt, 3) run eval.

-- Uma
